title: Gabber's affine comparison for a henselian pair
statement:
Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $Z=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ and $z:Z\to X$ the closed immersion. For every torsion abelian sheaf $F$ on $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf] the pullback map [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback]
$$
z^*:H^q(X_{\Et},F)\longrightarrow H^q(Z_{\Et},z^{-1}F)
$$
is an isomorphism for every $q\ge0$ ($H^q$ etale cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], $z^{-1}$ the inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]). Only the pair form is asserted: for an affine scheme of finite type over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ in place of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ the comparison with the closed fibre is false (see the report of lemma-weil-pbc-injective-restriction-acyclicity and the Lean docstring of AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.bijective_cohomologyMap_of_henselianRing).

source.lean: slopmaster2: AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.bijective_cohomologyMap_of_henselianRing, WeilConjectures/SixFunctors/Etale/Gabber.lean:227 (stated for torsion sheaves of Λ-modules; reaches sorry in bijective_cohomologyMap_zero_of_henselianRing and exists_mono_map_eq_zero_of_henselianRing)

proof.text: For degree $q=0$, the pullback map is the restriction map on sections. Apply the affine degree-zero comparison [lemma-weil-pbc-etale-degree-zero] to the proper identity morphism $\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ and the closed immersion $z:Z\to X$; it gives a bijection $H^0(X_{\Et},F)=\Gamma(X,F)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(Z,z^{-1}F)=H^0(Z_{\Et},z^{-1}F)$.

source.place: Theorem Tag 09ZI, proof opening sentence, using Lemma Tag 09ZH (59.82.6)

proof.text: Fix $q>0$ and assume the comparison is bijective in every smaller degree, for every torsion sheaf. Choose a monomorphism $\iota:F\hookrightarrow F'$ of torsion sheaves and write $Q=\operatorname{coker}(\iota)$. The resulting short exact sequence $0\to F\to F'\to Q\to0$ and its inverse image along $z$ give a commutative diagram of long exact cohomology sequences on $X$ and $Z$ [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-cohomology-long-exact-ladder]; the restriction map for $F'$ and $Q$ in degree $q-1$ is an isomorphism by the induction hypothesis.

source.place: Theorem Tag 09ZI (59.82.7), proof: short exact sequence and comparison diagram

proof.text: For injectivity, let $\xi\in H^q(X_{\Et},F)$ restrict to zero on $Z$. Apply affine Gabber effacement [lemma-weil-pbc-gabber-effacement] to the same class on the closed subscheme $X$ (the henselian pair $(A,0)$) to obtain a monomorphism $F\hookrightarrow F'$ for which the image of $\xi$ is zero. Exactness of the upper long exact sequence then writes $\xi$ as the image of a class in $H^{q-1}(X_{\Et},Q)$. The induction isomorphism for $Q$ identifies that class with a class on $Z$; commutativity of the ladder and exactness of the lower sequence show that the restriction of $\xi$ is nonzero whenever the chosen class is nonzero, hence the kernel is zero.

source.place: Theorem Tag 09ZI, proof: Injectivity for $\mathcal F$ (59.82.7)

proof.text: For surjectivity, let $\eta\in H^q(Z_{\Et},z^{-1}F)$. Apply the same effacement lemma to the class on $Z$ to obtain a monomorphism $F\hookrightarrow F'$ whose image of $\eta$ is zero, with cokernel $Q$. Exactness of the lower long exact sequence writes $\eta$ as the image of a class in $H^{q-1}(Z_{\Et},z^{-1}Q)$. By the induction isomorphism for $Q$, lift this class to $H^{q-1}(X_{\Et},Q)$; exactness of the upper sequence then produces a class in $H^q(X_{\Et},F)$ mapping to $\eta$. This proves surjectivity, and induction over all $q$ proves the comparison.

source.place: Theorem Tag 09ZI, proof: Surjectivity for $\mathcal F$ (59.82.7)

split_report.summary: Split the pair-form Gabber comparison by the proof of Stacks Tag 09ZI: degree zero via the existing affine degree-zero comparison, then induction on q using a torsion monomorphism with cokernel, the existing long-exact pullback ladder, and the existing affine effacement lemma for injectivity and surjectivity. The superseded relative finite-type statement remains excluded as documented in the statement.
